body_ar:
لما خلق الله البشر لم يتركهم عبثاً ولا أهملهم سدى، بل أرسل إليهم رسله ليخرجوهم من الظلمات إلى النور، وللأنبياء خصائص وصفات يجب أن تتوفر فيهم؛ تشريفاً من الله، وصيانة للرسالة، وإقامة للحجة.
الرسالة اجتباء لا اكتساب:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين. قال الشيخ حفظه الله: [والرسل حق والنبي العربي خاتمهم أعلاهم في الرتب] يريد بهذا بيان ركن آخر من أركان الإيمان وهو الإيمان برسل الله. والرسل جمع رسول، وهو من أوحي إليه بشرع وأمره بتبليغه، والرسول يختاره الله سبحانه وتعالى من الملائكة أو من الناس، كما قال تعالى: اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ النَّاسِ [الحج:75] ، لكن الرسل من الملائكة هم رسل إلى الرسل من البشر، وهذا نوع من أنواع الوحي، وقد سبق ذكر أنواع الوحي. والرسل من الملائكة كذلك يبلغون بعض الملائكة، ولهذا ذكر الله سبحان وتعالى أن الملائكة يسألون بعد أن يفزع عن قلوبهم إذا سمعوا كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى: حَتَّى إِذَا فُزِّعَ عَنْ قُلُوبِهِمْ قَالُوا مَاذَا قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ [سبأ:23]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* When God created human beings, He did not leave them to no purpose nor neglect them in vain; rather He sent His messengers to them, to bring them out of the darknesses into the light. The prophets have distinguishing features and qualities that must be present in them — as an ennobling from God, as a safeguarding of the message, and as the establishing of the proof against people.

## Messengerhood is a choosing by God, not something earned

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and God's blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions all together. The Sheikh, may God preserve him, said: *[And the messengers are true; and the Arabian Prophet is the seal of them, the highest of them in rank.]* By this he means to set out another of the pillars of faith, namely faith in God's messengers.

"Rusul" is the plural of "rasūl", and a messenger is one to whom a revealed law has been revealed and who has been commanded to convey it. God, glorified and exalted is He, chooses the messenger from among the angels or from among human beings, as He, exalted is He, said: {God chooses messengers from among the angels and from among people} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:75). But the messengers who are angels are messengers to the messengers who are human beings, and this is one of the kinds of revelation — and the kinds of revelation have already been mentioned. The messengers among the angels likewise convey to some of the angels, and for this reason God, glorified and exalted is He, mentioned that the angels ask, once the terror has been lifted from their hearts, when they hear the speech of God, glorified and exalted is He: {until, when the terror is lifted from their hearts, they say: what did your Lord say? They say: the truth. And He is the Most High, the Most Great} (Sūrat Sabaʾ 34:23) …

options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis while still defining the term 'messenger', before any of the 'distinguishing features and qualities' announced by the synopsis, and before the section heading's claim that messengerhood is a choosing rather than something earned, is argued at all. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-27.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified creed being commented on
options: read it as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Getting this referent wrong would misattribute a creedal formulation, so it is flagged on every record in which the formula appears. These lessons are a commentary on a versified creed (nazm): the transcriber introduces each base-text line with 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said', and the commentary follows. 'حفظه الله' is used of the living, which at first sight fits Sheikh al-Dedew himself. Three passages inside the run settle it otherwise. Record 719 has the speaker giving thanks for 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification' and describing what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed — a commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text that way while expounding it. Record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq by 'one of the scholars'. Record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh' is the living author of the versified base text and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named, and the identification should be confirmed by the Sheikh's office before publication, because the bracketed verse and the prose around it carry different attributions.

options: Messengerhood is a choosing by God, not something earned
Prophetic mission is bestowed, not acquired
Messengerhood is by divine selection, not by attainment
flags.note: The heading states a contested position in creed — that prophethood cannot be earned by effort — in four words, and the served text never returns to it. 'اجتباء' is God's singling out for Himself; 'اكتساب' is what a person acquires by his own action. The pairing is the whole point and the English keeps both nouns. A reader should be told that the record does not argue the claim.

flags.context: ولهذا ذكر الله سبحان وتعالى أن الملائكة يسألون
options: preserve as served and translate the evident formula
correct to سبحانه وتعالى in body_ar
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, style guide section 11. The honorific is served as 'سبحان وتعالى', missing the pronoun; the same formula is correct twice elsewhere in the same sentence. Preserved in body_ar and not repaired; body_en renders the evident formula.

flags.context: the definition of رسول in the transcribed portion
options: and who has been commanded to convey it
and who has been commanded to convey it, as against a prophet who has not
flags.note: The definition given turns on the command to convey, which is the classical criterion distinguishing a messenger (rasūl) from a prophet (nabī). The Sheikh does not draw that contrast in the served text and the English does not supply it, per style guide section 6. Recorded here because a reader who knows the distinction will expect it and must not be given it by the translator.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The bracketed line is a line of the versified creed being commented on. Per style guide section 4 it is rendered as prose in italics and no rhymed English has been attempted; the Arabic is kept in body_ar for the bilingual pane.
The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, so that the quoted verse and its commentary are visibly separated. No word has been added or removed.
No ruling term from the five-rulings table appears anywhere in the record.
